I will do it close to what I have done in recent years, then adjust a little by looking at water, fertilizer price, and what grows well around me. On my 7 mu, wheat and maize are linked together, so if I spend too much on one crop, the next crop gets tight on money. I have well irrigation, so I do not want to save too much on water or fertilizer and then lose yield. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put a solid base fertilizer before sowing, then topdress nitrogen when the seedlings turn and jointing starts. Around here, if wheat fertilizer is too light, the heads are small and the grains are not full. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, because that is what most people around me plant and the yield is steadier. I will give maize enough nitrogen, with some phosphorus and potassium underneath, then another nitrogen topdressing around the big flare stage. I will still watch costs, but fertilizer is cheaper than a bad harvest, so I would rather put a bit more than a bit less. With irrigation from the well, normal pest spraying, and rotary tillage for convenience, I will aim for a steady wheat-maize harvest this year.
